source.title: Should Under-parameterized Student Networks Copy or Average Teacher Weights?
source.authors: Berfin Şimşek; Amire Bendjeddou; W. Gerstner; Johanni Brea

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper through its appendices; no truncation or garbling that prevents reading the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own gradient-flow experiments on under-parameterized student networks and outcomes at convergence, using a Gaussian teacher–student population-loss setup rather than the benchmark classification-error recipes in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study tests gradient-flow convergence and loss for under-parameterized students learning from unit-orthonormal teacher networks. These are population squared-loss approximation results, not CIFAR classification error. One-neuron and copy-average theory results are recorded only where they state outcomes about the tested optimization problem. Cited results from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern approximation and convergence for under-parameterized shallow students, where a perfect teacher match is unavailable. They do not test V2's realizable ReLU setting or extra-width comparison, or any other version. Spurious minima at equal teacher–student width are attributed to prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. For unit-orthonormal teachers and Gaussian inputs, the authors characterize erf copy-average critical points and prove which configuration minimizes loss within that family. Gradient flow reaches this configuration under stronger compression and perturbed-copy configurations under weaker compression; ReLU shows qualitative similarities. Global optimality of the best copy-average configuration is conjectured only in a restricted regime, not proved generally.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses gradient flow on a two-layer teacher–student population squared-loss problem with Gaussian inputs and orthogonal teacher vectors. It does not use the benchmark classification-error training recipes in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on student-to-teacher width ratio and activation: erf shows copy-average or perturbed n-copy regimes; ReLU configurations are qualitatively similar but not perfectly decoupled. Some ReLU seeds fail to converge.

fits_no_version.finding: One-neuron students converge to averaging solutions across several activations; erf and ReLU admit explicit optimal parameters and population approximation losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For one-neuron students approximating unit-orthonormal teachers under Gaussian inputs, optimal solutions align equally with teacher vectors, with explicit solutions for erf and ReLU.

fits_no_version.finding: Under-parameterized erf students reach copy-average or perturbed-copy configurations depending on width ratio; near teacher width, perturbed-copy solutions can have lower loss than every copy-average configuration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The configurations reached by gradient flow in under-parameterized erf teacher–student networks vary with compression ratio.

fits_no_version.finding: Successful under-parameterized ReLU runs reach configurations qualitatively resembling the erf configurations, without exact decoupling; an unspecified fraction of runs fails to converge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under-parameterized ReLU teacher–student gradient flow exhibits width-dependent configuration structure and occasional convergence failures.

record.peer_reviewed: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)
record.problems: The evidence is for an idealized Gaussian-input, orthogonal-teacher population squared-loss setup, not benchmark classification error. Multi-neuron order-parameter optimization is a relaxation for n ≥ 3. ReLU experiments report only successful converged seeds for configuration results, and Figure 4 numerical means are not stated in prose.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results were omitted. Figure-only numerical means and correlation-matrix values were not reconstructed from plots; the qualitative results described in text are recorded in rows R2–R6.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional classification training error on CIFAR, including corrupted labels, optimizer recipes, and size or stopping conditions.
All parts: spurious-minimum frequency in realizable ReLU teacher–student problems, jointly increasing widths, and adding one or two student neurons beyond teacher width.
All parts: depth degradation, identity shortcuts, deep plain-network initialization, and normalization-free residual training.

All parts: initialization comparisons for speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth. Using Gaussian or Glorot initialization without reporting their comparative effects does not test this version.
All parts: finite learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, sharpness trajectories, and divergence.
All parts: batch normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the supplied claim versions because every row links to none; this does not negate the study's reported findings. Citations to Safran and Shamir and use of Glorot initialization supply no independent test of V2 or V4.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error; random or corrupted labels; convolutional benchmarks; SGD or Adam recipes; model-size and training-duration regimes from the version.

Teacher–student ReLU spurious-local-minimum frequency as teacher and student widths grow together, and the effect of adding one or two student neurons beyond teacher width. This paper studies under-parameterized students with erf or ReLU, not that over-parameterized width comparison.
Plain versus residual shortcut networks at depth on ImageNet or CIFAR-10, and training outcomes with the special plain-network or normalization-free residual recipes.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization at equal variance for deep tanh networks, and 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Learning rates above stability thresholds, curvature or sharpness trajectories, and divergence under full-batch training.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for speed or learning-rate tolerance on MNIST, CIFAR-10, or ImageNet, and Fixup residual training.

rows.subject: student network, n = 1
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flow from random initialization on population squared loss against a unit-orthonormal teacher.

conditions.value: Gaussian with zero mean and standard deviation 0.1 or Glorot initialization
105 ode iterations for erf and relu; 103 ode iterations for softplus, tanh, and sigmoid

rows.measure: Convergence to the same optimal one-neuron solution up to symmetries; for ReLU, magnitude matches the stated formula.
rows.value: All students converge to the same optimal solution up to symmetries; ReLU magnitude exactly matches Corollary G.5.
rows.note: This is population approximation loss, not training classification error. The sentence reports all seeds converging; Appendix C says the erf seeds have gradient norm below 5 · 10−8, while the convergence description in Figure 5 covers the listed activations.
rows.check: One-neuron population-loss convergence does not measure any version. Figure 5 reports convergence across activations, but Appendix C also reports unspecified ReLU convergence failures; avoid extending the all-seeds statement to all ReLU experiments. Iteration counts are 10^5 and 10^3.

rows.subject: student network, width n; teacher network, width k
rows.size_stated: n < k; experiments include n = 2, 4, 8 and k = 64
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flow from Gaussian random initialization on population squared loss with erf activation.

conditions.value: Gaussian with zero mean and standard deviation 0.1 or Glorot initialization
n < γ1 k, with γ1 near 0.46

rows.measure: Type of convergence point and mean loss at convergence.
rows.baseline: Theory prediction L*erf(k−n+1); no separate initialization-free baseline stated.
rows.value: Converges to an optimal (n − 1)-copy-1-average solution for all 20 initializations in the green regime.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations do not show on the figure as they are too small.
rows.note: The study describes this as a regime of under-parameterization and reports population loss, not classification error. Figure 4's individual numerical means are figure-only.
rows.check: Convergence to the best copy-average configuration does not establish global optimality among all configurations; that broader claim is conjectured in a restricted width regime. This erf result does not test V2.

rows.subject: student network, width n; teacher network, width k
rows.size_stated: n < k; n = 8, 12, 16 are named for the threshold observation
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flow from Gaussian random initialization on population squared loss with erf activation.

conditions.value: n > γ1 k, with γ1 near 0.46; some seeds

rows.baseline: Optimal (n − 1)-copy-1-average point is the comparison configuration.
rows.value: Some seeds converge to points close to the n-copy critical point, called perturbed n-copy (P-n-C).
rows.note: The text says this occurs only when n > γ1 k for n = 8, 12, 16; it does not provide per-seed counts in text.
rows.check: Some erf seeds reaching perturbed-copy points is outside all versions. A subset of seeds displaying this configuration does not itself warrant a partial state for a claim version.

rows.subject: student network, width n; teacher network, width k
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flow from Gaussian random initialization on population squared loss with erf activation.

conditions.value: n > γ2 k, with γ2 near 0.6

rows.value: Converges to a perturbed n-copy point for all seeds.
rows.note: This describes the low-compression regime of the paper's idealized population squared-loss experiments.
rows.check: All-seed convergence to perturbed-copy configurations in under-parameterized erf networks measures none of the versions.

rows.subject: student network, width n; teacher network, width k
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flow from Gaussian random initialization on population squared loss with erf activation.

conditions.value: n > γ3 k, with γ3 near 0.75

rows.measure: P-n-C loss compared with the loss of the (n − 1)-copy-1-average solution.
rows.value: P-n-C solutions achieve lower loss than the (n − 1)-copy-1-average solutions.
rows.note: The text calls the loss difference slight in the low-compression regime. Numerical values for individual seeds are figure-only.
rows.check: Relative approximation loss of two under-parameterized erf configurations measures none of the versions.

rows.subject: student network, width n; teacher network, width k
rows.size_stated: n = 2, 4, 12; k values shown in Figure 9
rows.operation_detail: Gradient flow on population squared loss with ReLU activation.

conditions.value: Figure 9 panels show n = 2 with k = 5, 10, 20; n = 4 with k = 5, 8, 16; n = 12 with k = 16, 24, 32

rows.measure: Structure of the minimum-loss configuration found by gradient flow.
rows.value: For n ≪ k, configurations are qualitatively similar to optimal-CA but without perfect decoupling; when k is slightly bigger than n, n = 4, 12 find an all-copy configuration.
rows.uncertainty: A fraction of ReLU seeds failed to converge; reported among seeds that succeeded.
rows.note: Appendix C.3 gives qualitative configuration descriptions; correlation matrices in Figure 9 are not transcribed as precise numeric values.
rows.check: ReLU configuration structure among successful under-parameterized runs cannot establish spurious-minimum frequency in V2's realizable regime. Figure 9 specifically finds perturbed all-copy configurations at (n,k) = (4,5), (12,16), and (12,24); convergence failures are not quantified.

rows.subject: student network, width n = 1
rows.operation_detail: Analytical characterization of non-trivial critical points for erf population squared loss.
rows.measure: Optimal incoming-vector norm, outgoing weight, and normalized alignment with teacher vectors.
rows.value: ∥w*∥ = 1/√(2k − 1); a* = √k; w*/∥w*∥ = (1/√k)∑ᵢvᵢ; optimal loss L*erf(k) = (2/π)(k arcsin(1/2) − k² arcsin(1/(2k))).
rows.note: The theorem is about population squared-loss approximation and its critical points.
rows.check: The outgoing weight is a* = k, not sqrt(k), in Corollary 5.2 and Equation 16. The remaining formula describes approximation geometry, outside all versions. Appendix G.3 relies on numerical evidence for uniqueness.

rows.subject: student network, width n = 1
rows.operation_detail: Analytical characterization of non-trivial critical points for ReLU population squared loss.
rows.measure: Optimal product of incoming norm and outgoing weight, direction, and optimal loss.
rows.note: ReLU's positive homogeneity gives an equal-loss hyperbola; the result concerns population squared loss.
rows.check: The analytical one-neuron ReLU optimum and approximation loss measure none of the versions; they do not test extra student width or convergence frequencies.
